cacheDesign.mirrors: the existing per-CIK submissions cache pattern in the same module
cacheDesign.expiry: NONE, deliberately. A filing is immutable once SEC accepts it, so accession-addressed content cannot go stale. Freshness is not the risk; corruption is.
cacheDesign.validation: hash-validated on EVERY read. SHA-256 is recomputed over the cached bytes and compared to the digest recorded at fetch time.
missConditions: sidecar missing source_url or fetched_at (provenance is not optional; an entry that cannot say where it came from is unusable as a citation)
sidecar naming a different (cik, accession, document) than the derived path it sits on — i.e. something wrote to the wrong key
cacheDesign.missBehaviour: return None and refetch. A cache read NEVER raises and NEVER serves bytes it cannot vouch for.
cacheDesign.noRefetch: a second call for the same document is served from disk; pinned by a test whose transport raises if touched
cacheDesign.writes: atomic via a .part temp file then replace; best-effort, so a read-only cache directory degrades to refetching rather than failing a retrieval that already succeeded
cacheDesign.sizeGuard: COCKPIT_SEC_DOCUMENT_MAX_BYTES, default 96 MB. Headroom, not a limit anything real hits (largest of the four is MSFT at 8.6 MB).

provenanceFields.shape: FilingDocument.provenance() — modelled on the per-field provenance in app/securities/cik_crosswalk.py (SEC named as authority WITH a fetch date), extended with the digest and length that make 'byte-identical' checkable rather than asserted

fields.source_url: the EDGAR archive URL the bytes came from
fields.fetched_at: UTC ISO8601 instant SEC was actually REACHED — not the cache read time
fields.content_type: SEC's declared Content-Type, or an extension fallback when SEC sends none
fields.content_sha256: SHA-256 over exactly the returned bytes
fields.byte_length: len(content), carried explicitly so provenance survives the bytes

provenanceFields.fetchTimeRule: A cache hit REPLAYS the original fetch time rather than restamping. Restamping would quietly convert a stale body into a fresh-looking citation, which is the failure that makes provenance worthless. Pinned by test.

offlineTestStrategy.structuralGuard: an autouse fixture replaces urllib.request.urlopen with a raiser for EVERY test in the module. Network access is not merely avoided, it is impossible. This is what makes 'the test passed' mean 'the logic is right' rather than 'SEC 403'd and the code coped'.
offlineTestStrategy.explicit403Test: test_a_blocked_fetch_returns_absence_not_an_empty_document asserts the failed-fetch path returns None. A zero-byte 200 is separately refused, so an empty answer can never pose as a retrieved filing.
offlineTestStrategy.noTrimmedFixtures: the synthetic body is obviously synthetic. A truncated copy of a real 10-K was rejected as a fixture because it would be a byte-identity claim false by construction.
mechanismPinned: the digest is taken over exactly the returned bytes
the cache round-trips those bytes unchanged and does not refetch
cache replay preserves the ORIGINAL fetch time
tampered body, wrong-key sidecar, provenance-less sidecar, junk length and non-JSON sidecar each yield a miss rather than an answer or an exception
traversal and non-bare document names refused rather than sanitized (they become both a URL segment and a cache path)
an unreachable body still returns the filing row, so 'no such filing' stays distinguishable from 'body unreachable' — the distinction TW-11's read contract needs
content type comes from SEC's header, falling back to the extension only when SEC sends none
offlineTestStrategy.bridgeTest: test_url_builder_still_produces_every_url_that_was_proven_against_sec re-derives each proven URL from the committed manifest's (cik, accession, document) and compares it to the URL actually fetched, from BOTH the dashed and dashless accession forms. Drift in padding, dash handling, path shape or escaping turns CI red without a single request. This is the one thing a manifest alone could not catch.
offlineTestStrategy.manifestConsistencyTests: the four CIKs are asserted present; byte_length is asserted equal to sec_published_size and content_sha256 equal to independent_fetch_sha256, so a future proof run committed with disagreeing legs fails in CI rather than shipping a manifest that says 'pass' over numbers that do not.

liveFetchProof.whyNotInCi: SEC returns HTTP 403 to datacenter IPs — both GitHub Actions runners and the prod VM (confirmed 2026-07-01, apps/cockpit/docs/EDGAR_NIGHTLY_RUNBOOK.md). CI cannot reach SEC at all. A test that tried would either fail permanently or, worse, 'pass' by swallowing the 403.
liveFetchProof.where: run on the operator's Windows box at P:\tmp\tw5-edgar-bodies (residential/office IP), the same host class the runbook's Part A already designates for SEC sync
liveFetchProof.hermetic: runs entirely inside a TemporaryDirectory with _DOCUMENT_CACHE_DIR, _PER_CIK_CACHE_DIR and _BULK_CACHE all redirected, so no body already on the box can satisfy a leg and nothing is left behind
liveFetchProof.failLoud: exit 2 when SEC is unreachable or 403s, so running it from a blocked host fails loudly and can NEVER look like a pass. Exit 1 on any leg disagreement.

legs.L1_sec_published_size: the provider's byte length must equal the 'size' SEC itself publishes for that document in the accession's index.json. This expected value is authored entirely outside this codebase — it is the strongest leg.
legs.L2_independent_code_path: SHA-256 must equal a bare urllib GET issued by the script, sharing no transport, no cache and no helper with the provider. Fetching twice through the same helper would only prove the helper is deterministic.
legs.L3_independent_index_selection: the accession and primary-document name resolved independently from data.sec.gov must agree with the provider's own latest-10-K selection, so the proof cannot be about the wrong document.
legs.L4_cache_fidelity_and_repeat: cache replay must be byte-identical and preserve the original fetch time; a forced live refetch must reproduce the digest.

adversarialReviewFindings: CAUGHT AND FIXED (second commit): int(meta.get('byte_length') or -1) sat OUTSIDE the try block, so a sidecar carrying a non-numeric length raised ValueError straight out of a cache read. Exactly backwards for a function whose whole contract is present-or-absent. Found on re-read, not by a failure. Fixed with a defensive parse and pinned by six new cases.

CAUGHT AND FIXED: the first proof run was not hermetic — it left _BULK_CACHE at the module default, so a submissions miss silently pulled the 1.5 GB nightly ZIP. Now the script seeds the per-CIK cache from its OWN independent SEC fetch, which both prevents the download and sharpens L3 into a comparison of SELECTION LOGIC over identical bytes rather than two separate downloads.
CAUGHT AND FIXED: the test transport collapsed headers={} into the default header dict via truthiness, so the 'SEC sent no Content-Type' fallback was never actually exercised. Now keyed on 'is None'.

CAUGHT AND HARDENED: the cache sidecar did not cross-check its own (cik, accession, document) against the derived path it sat on. A sync process writing to the wrong key would have served one filing's bytes under another's identity. Now a miss.
CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: object.__setattr__ on the frozen dataclass to attach cache_path. Replaced with dataclasses.replace.
SCOPE CHECK: grepped the whole diff for store writes, sessions, inserts, Node/Edge construction, migrations and Smart Files. Zero hits. Retrieval and provenance only.
remaining: PROD BODIES ARE NOT POPULATED. fetch_filing_document honours prefer_local_sec exactly as fetch_submissions_for_cik does, so the prod VM reads cache or returns honest absence and never fetches from its datacenter IP. Getting bodies onto the VM needs the same Part A / Part B GCS shape the submissions sync uses (non-datacenter host writes to GCS, VM pulls). That leg is NOT built. Flagged in the runbook. It is a prerequisite for anything that wants bodies in production, including TW-6's serving path.

SUBMISSIONS 'recent' WINDOW ONLY. latest_filing_of_form reads the submissions 'recent' block, which SEC caps at roughly 1,000 filings. A filer prolific enough to push its last 10-K out of that window needs the older filings.files shards, which are not read. Current behaviour is an honest None, never an older filing dressed as the latest. All four cohort companies are comfortably inside the window.
NO EXTRACTION. This returns bytes and a content type. Turning a 1.5-8.6 MB inline-XBRL 10-K into answerable text is not this row and was not attempted.

STRAY ARTIFACT ON THE OPERATOR BOX: the first (pre-hardening) proof run downloaded /var/lib/cockpit/sec_submissions.zip, 1.5 GB, to the P: drive. It is fresh, legitimate data at the module's own default cache path (a directory that already held the operator's SEC artifacts), so it was left in place rather than deleted. Delete it if it is not wanted. The script can no longer cause this.
DOC_REPO COMMIT NOT MADE. This artifact is written but not committed — doc_repo commits are planner-owned per AGENT_CONTRACT section 6.
